kept.heading: ORGANIC TRAFFIC IS DOWN, BUT IT'S NOT ALL AI (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Organic search traffic fell 13% in the US and 24% in France over two years, but losses vary by industry and site size. Publishers lost about 42% of organic traffic in both markets, while smaller sites remained roughly flat. Paid search traffic grew 21% in the US as larger ad blocks pushed organic results below the fold. AI referrals account for just 0.5% of total visits, suggesting that AI alone doesn't explain declining search traffic.

kept.heading: THE END OF THE INTERNET (11 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The internet's shift from open blogs and social networks to algorithm-driven platforms has made discovery harder and independent businesses less sustainable. AI could accelerate this decline by flooding the web with content and creating more security risks. Smaller communities and businesses offer an alternative. Paid niche publications can thrive on loyal readers while private group chats build stronger connections. AI also makes it easier to create custom apps for individuals or small teams without needing mass-market demand.

kept.heading: STEAL YOUR COMPETITOR'S CUSTOMERS FOR <$100 (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Wispr Flow pays $35 for every paying Granola user who switches, covering their remaining subscription and adding 3 free months. The strategy recruits competitor affiliates by offering higher referral payouts. Existing customers can also refer contacts who use rivals, while sales teams can re-engage prospects who chose a competitor earlier in the year. Covering the remainder of their subscription reduces switching costs and gives them a reason to reconsider.

kept.heading: GET THE FREE PLAYBOOK
MEET CLAUDE, YOUR NEW VIDEO EDITOR (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A free kit of 30 Claude Code skills turns the model into a local video editor using ffmpeg and Python, with no paid APIs. It includes 18 motion effects and 12 editing tools that identify strong hooks from long recordings, cutting a 40-sec clip from a 60-min episode in 2 minutes. The tools also interpret spoken editing notes to select takes and refine cuts. Effects are designed for head-and-shoulders footage and take up to 5 minutes to render.

kept.heading: PINTEREST UNLOCKS PREMIUM INVENTORY FOR PROGRAMMATIC BUYERS, SCALING HIGH-INTENT DISCOVERY (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Pinterest has made Programmatic Deals widely available in select markets, letting advertisers buy its video and display inventory through platforms like Amazon Ads and Google Display & Video 360. The move gives brands easier access to Pinterest's high-intent audience within existing media plans. The platform now reaches 640M monthly users.

kept.heading: IN A ZERO-CLICK WORLD, YOUR BEST MARKETING DOESN'T SHOW UP IN YOUR ANALYTICS (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: In a zero-click world, last-click attribution misses the content that builds trust long before a purchase. Tutorials and videos can influence buyers for years without getting credit for the sale. Talk directly to customers to learn what convinced them to buy and what keeps them loyal. Use AI to analyze their responses and uncover what your metrics miss.

kept.heading: LEGO AND DAFT PUNK'S TEAM-UP HIGHLIGHTS EXACTLY HOW BRANDS SHOULD INTERACT WITH FANS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: LEGO built its Daft Punk collaboration around fan participation by turning a fan-designed set into a product after it won a LEGO Ideas contest and gained 10K supporters. It teased the partnership with a cryptic video that encouraged fans to decode and discuss the reveal. The launch film blended both brands' visual styles without letting either dominate. Rather than rush out products, LEGO treats the partnership as a long-term relationship with its audience.

kept.heading: META'S SOCIAL APPS ARE GROWING. AI RECOMMENDATIONS ARE WHY. (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Feeds on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads now run more on AI predictions of what users want than on the accounts they follow.

kept.heading: 3 REASONS TO JOIN:
kept.blurb: >Get into why Sales rolls their eyes at “accounts with intent.”

kept.heading: REGISTER FOR THE FIRST LOOK ON NOV 5.
GROWING SHARE OF AMERICANS SAY SOCIAL MEDIA IS AN IMPORTANT NEWS SOURCE FOR THEM (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 58% of US adults say social media is important for keeping up with the news, up from 43% in 2022. Among adults ages 18-29, that figure rises to 76%, including 22% who say social media is their most important news source. 41% of adults 65 and older feel the same.

kept.heading: DO HOLIDAY OFFERS BRING SUBSCRIPTION APPS MORE THAN A SALES SPIKE? (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Subscription apps running Black Friday promotions get 20% more new paying customers per day than their autumn baseline, while apps without offers get 16% fewer. Each discounted buyer is worth 8% less over six months, but the extra volume leaves sale-day revenue 12% higher. About half the lift comes from free users who installed the app more than three months earlier. Christmas-only offers show no advantage, while New Year promotions drive 14% more new paying customers, led by fitness and gaming apps.

kept.heading: HOW TO TURN WEBINARS INTO PIPELINE BEFORE YOU EVER GO LIVE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: After someone registers for a webinar, use the thank-you page to ask 5-6 questions about their role, challenges, and needs. This turns registration into a lead qualification flow before the event even happens. Use the answers to personalize follow-up offers and let high-intent prospects book demos immediately. About 90% of registrants complete the extra questions.

kept.heading: UNDERSTORY: B2B LINKEDIN SWIPE LIBRARY (WEBSITE)
kept.blurb: A swipe library of 42 B2B LinkedIn ads, selected from 13,483 unique creatives across 251 advertisers. It breaks down 14 proven ad formats with real examples and guidance on visuals, headlines, copy, and CTAs.

kept.heading: WATCH OUT, YOUTUBE - INSTAGRAM GOES FROM SHORT-FORM TO 90-MINUTE VIDEOS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Instagram is testing “Features”, allowing creators to upload videos up to 90 minutes long as it looks to compete with YouTube and keep audiences on its platform. It's also testing tools that turn long videos into Reels that link to the full version. This could create new ways for creators to earn money through ads and fan payments.

kept.heading: HOW TO WORK BETTER WITH AI ON YOUR TEAM (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A study found that people working with AI and a colleague produced higher-quality solutions than people working alone. Participants performed 10.2% better when they worked with both AI and a colleague, compared with 9.6% better with AI alone and 6.3% better with a colleague alone. They were also roughly 3x more likely to rank among the top performers according to expert evaluations. The benefits disappeared when teammates had the same skills, suggesting that complementary expertise helps people and AI work together more effectively.

kept.heading: OPENAI'S STRONGEST CHANNEL FOR SELLING CHATGPT TO BUSINESSES IS IN-PERSON EVENTS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI has more product awareness than any company in its category, and yet it still relies on getting buyers into a room. In-person events are its strongest channel for selling ChatGPT to businesses because enterprise purchases require buy-in from multiple executives. Product awareness alone doesn't address concerns about data security, costs, employee training, and deployment across large organizations. OpenAI also uses a fixed marketing calendar that incorporates new product launches into recurring activities, including about two webinars per month, rather than building a separate campaign for each release.

kept.heading: WHY BELLIWELLI'S CO-FOUNDER AND CEO IS FILMING SKITS IN WALMART AT NIGHT (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: BelliWelli's CEO treats short-form production as core to her job because the skits drive so much of the brand's retail traffic. The improvised Walmart scenes, staged with about 65 rotating actors, show shoppers fighting over the fiber supplement so viewers wonder why it's in such demand. The videos run organically, not as ads, and the brand leans into cringe because it gets noticed. Filming in stores also gives Wilson regular conversations with shoppers about what they reach for in the category.

kept.heading: IS AI VISIBILITY A MARKETING BOONDOGGLE? (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI visibility may influence brand awareness, but its traffic and conversion impact remains tiny compared with Google.

kept.heading: SOCIAL ROULETTE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Social platforms are reintroducing randomness to help people meet new people and make unexpected connections.

kept.heading: X HAS A CREEPY NEW WAY TO MAKE YOU PROMOTE YOUR POSTS, AND NOBODY ASKED FOR IT (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: X is testing a floating hand that points users toward the Promote button, nudging them to pay to boost their posts.

kept.heading: CHATBOTS PUT PR BACK ON THE BRAND AGENDA. SOCIAL LISTENING DECIDES WHAT IT SHOULD SAY (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI search is giving PR a larger role in marketing because chatbots use third-party coverage to answer questions and recommend brands. One forecast projects that PR and earned media budgets will double by 2027 as more consumers use AI chatbots instead of traditional search. Social listening also gives brands real-time audience research, helping teams identify which creative ideas resonate and which risk backlash before investing further. As AI makes content cheaper to produce, audience understanding and independent brand credibility become more valuable.

kept.heading: OZEMPIC IS CHANGING HOW AMERICANS SPEND MONEY, AND THE NUMBERS ARE STARTLING (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are reshaping consumer spending across food, fitness, and retail. 11% of American adults use these medications, with 26% of users spending more on clothing and 36% more on jewelry. Meanwhile, household spending at fast-food restaurants drops nearly 9% after 6-8 months on the drugs. Users are also buying fewer sweets and sugary drinks while spending more on fresh produce and protein.

kept.heading: SPOTTING CTR DECAY EARLY: HOW TO CATCH AD CREATIVE FATIGUE (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Creative fatigue shows up as one ad's CTR sliding week after week below its own launch-week level while frequency climbs and the other ads in the same ad set hold steady. A single early drop that then flattens is normal settling, not fatigue. CPM rising on every ad at once points to the auction or the calendar instead, and frequency rising while reach plateaus points to an exhausted audience. Meta's own “Creative fatigue” status only appears once cost per result doubles, well after spend is lost.

kept.heading: HOW TO WIN BFCM (WEBINAR)
kept.blurb: Verbose's Lifecycle Live workshop brings together lifecycle marketing experts to share BFCM campaign strategies. Joined by Hightouch's Luke Kline, the session covers contingency planning and cross-channel messaging. Attendees will learn how to drive customer engagement and long-term value beyond discounts.

kept.heading: THE EVOLUTION OF WEB SERIES ON YOUTUBE: MICRODRAMAS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Creators are turning Shorts into serialized dramas with short episodes and audience-driven storylines. YouTube is adding tools to organize episodes into series and improve discovery. New monetization options will also let creators offer members-only episodes. Brands can partner with creators to integrate products into these short-form stories.

kept.heading: THIRD-PARTY CITATION OPTIMIZATION PRIORITIZATION IN AN AI SEARCH ERA: A FRAMEWORK WITH WORKSHEET & CLAUDE SKILL (15 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: This guide shares a framework for prioritizing third-party websites that influence AI search recommendations. It scores opportunities across 6 criteria, including citation influence, brand association, and business value. The guide includes a worksheet and a Claude skill to identify valuable targets such as independent reviews and comparison guides.

kept.heading: THE ANATOMY OF THE BEST-PERFORMING ONBOARDING PAYWALLS (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Multi-page onboarding paywalls convert 47% better than single-page ones, and conversion peaks at 3 screens. The top performers follow the same sequence, a free-trial promise with no prices, then a trial-end reminder, then the offer. The reminder screen is the strongest single signal, lifting conversion from 8.7% to 14.8% by removing the fear of forgetting to cancel. Leading with one yearly plan beats the common yearly-plus-monthly picker by about 1.5x, and an abandon offer for users who cancel checkout adds roughly 18% revenue per view.

kept.heading: HOW WE BUILT AND LAUNCHED A VIRAL RESEARCH CAMPAIGN IN PARTNERSHIP WITH LINKEDIN (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Partnering with a brand that has complementary data and a shared interest can make original research stand out in a crowded market and expand its reach. Semrush combined its AI citation data with LinkedIn's content and engagement data to analyze around 89,000 LinkedIn URLs cited by AI search tools. The study found that 95% of cited posts were original content rather than reshares, and most cited posts averaged just 15 to 25 reactions. Semrush and LinkedIn coordinated media outreach, employee advocacy, social promotion, and launch timing to reach both audiences and generate strong media coverage, tens of thousands of visits, and dozens of signups. The collaboration also created new opportunities for guest content and speaking engagements beyond the initial campaign.

kept.heading: TIKTOK EXPANDS INTO RESTAURANT GUIDES WITH ‘MUST EAT' FEATURE (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The guide pulls recommendations from more than 40 million posts and comments into city lists filterable by cuisine, price, and location, with OpenTable booking for select restaurants.

kept.heading: GEO DOESN'T CREATE DEMAND. IT CAPTURES DEMAND THAT ALREADY EXISTS. (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI answers also only reach buyers already in-market, yet GEO is often judged like a performance channel.
